Web design in Spokane, WA has a question to settle before anything else: which Spokane? A customer on the South Hill, a family in Spokane Valley and a contractor driving over from Post Falls may all type the same city name, and each wants to know whether you are close enough to bother calling. A site that answers that in the first screen gets the call. One that leaves it vague sends people back to the search results.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, who writes every page by hand. You see a free demo first, and the price is paid once: $497, $997 or $1,997.

Spokane web design for two cities that share one name

Spokane Valley was unincorporated county land for more than a century. Voters narrowly approved becoming a city on May 21, 2002, after several failed attempts in the 1990s, and the new city officially began on March 31, 2003. The city says it is now home to more than 100,000 people, a city in its own right next door to Spokane.

That history matters for your site. Many people say "the Valley" and search that way. A roofer based in the Valley and a dentist downtown are both "Spokane" to someone in Seattle, but not to their neighbors. Say where you are by city name, and list the areas you cover by the names locals use.

Customers who drive in from the back country

Spokane draws people from a wide stretch of eastern Washington and north Idaho, especially for health care. The City of Spokane Valley calls the region the health care hub of the Inland Northwest and northern Idaho, with the largest concentration of medical services in four states.

They plan the trip

A family coming in from a small town for an appointment wants a place to eat, a pharmacy or a repair shop near the hospital, and they check before they leave home. Hours, parking and the nearest cross streets belong near the top of your page.

They come from Idaho too

Coeur d'Alene and Post Falls are across the state line in north Idaho. If you take customers or jobs from north Idaho, name those towns. If you work only in Washington, say that, so nobody calls from the wrong side of the border.

They call ahead

When the drive is long, people phone first. The number should dial with one tap from every page, and the site should say what to have ready: a part number, photos of the job, the size of the order.

Spokane website design that knows the districts

Spokane is a city of distinct districts, and naming yours helps a nearby customer recognize you as local. Browne's Addition, just west of downtown, is often called the city's oldest neighborhood and has a historic district on the National Register of Historic Places. The Garland District, north of downtown, is a commercial strip anchored by the 1940s-era Garland Theater. The South Perry District has a main street of cafes and shops and a weekly farmers market.

Kendall Yards shows how fast parts of the city change. Union Pacific used the land just north of downtown as a rail facility from 1914 to 1955, then it sat vacant for decades. The mixed-use neighborhood project got moving again in 2010 after stalling in the recession, and it now mixes shops, apartments and houses. A business that opened there recently has to introduce itself to customers who still remember an empty lot.

Downtown, Riverfront Park sits on the grounds of Expo '74, the world's fair that ran from May to November 1974 and drew more than 5 million visitors. The site was dedicated as Riverfront Park in 1978, and big events like Bloomsday and Hoopfest still bring crowds to the area. Those weekends bring crowds downtown, and a restaurant or shop nearby benefits from a site that shows event-day hours.

Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence. You control the first by describing your services clearly, and you make distance easy to judge by naming your district and the areas you serve. Fairchild Air Force Base is named in state profiles as Spokane County's largest employer, and Gonzaga University sits just north of downtown, so base families and students are part of the customer mix too.

Where Spokane owners can get free advice

  • Washington Small Business Development Center. The statewide network, a partnership of Washington State University and the U.S. Small Business Administration, has its lead center and advising offices at The Quarry in Spokane Valley. Advising is free and confidential, and it also runs low-cost workshops and market research.
  • Greater Spokane Inc. The region's chamber of commerce and economic development group in one. It works on advocacy, business growth and workforce programs.

Common questions

How much does Spokane website design cost?

It depends on who you hire and how they bill, so get the full first-year number in writing. Ours is printed: Starter $497, Pro $997, Agency $1,997, each paid one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent ($297 a month after its free trial). You see a free demo of your site before paying anything.

Should a business in Spokane Valley have different web design than one in Spokane?

The design can be the same; the words should not. Spokane Valley has been its own city since 2003, and people there often search with the Valley name. If you are based in the Valley, say so on the home page and the contact page. If you serve both cities, say that too, and give each its own section or page so the details are true for each one.

How often should a website be redesigned?

There is no fixed schedule. Redesign when the site no longer matches the business: your services changed, it is hard to use on a phone, it loads slowly, or you are embarrassed to send people to it. Small updates such as hours, prices and photos should happen whenever they change, and with us those are part of maintenance.

How do I find the best web design in Spokane for a small business?

Ask to see something built for your business before you pay, ask for every monthly charge in writing, and ask who will actually write your pages. A designer who answers those three plainly is a good start. Our answers: a free demo first, the prices on this page, and Maurice Johnson writes every page himself.

Ready to see a Spokane site that names the right side of town?

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
